title: In 1907, Austria's emperor gifted chamois to New Zealand; the mountain animals spread through the South Island, browsing fragile alpine vegetation | World News
text:
What chamois really eat
Parkes and Forsyth studied the diets of 78 chamois collected in the central Southern Alps from 1988 to 1996, so the data is decades old and today's diets and numbers may differ. They also looked at 246 Himalayan tahr and 113 brushtail possums. None of these three animals is native to New Zealand, and the paper states that the Department of Conservation manages all of them as pests. The team found that the chamois and tahr ate a lot of the same things. Tahr still ate more grasses, and chamois more herbs and woody plants. The food habits of all three animals also changed with the seasons.
